html:
Japan ruled Taiwan as its first colony for fifty years, from the Treaty of Shimonoseki in 1895 to the end of the Second World War in 1945.

Local resistance, including a short-lived Republic of Formosa, was crushed in 1895, and armed revolts went on for years. The colonial government then built railways, ports, dams and schools, ran public health campaigns and made the island a supplier of rice and sugar to Japan. In the Wushe incident of 1930 it put down an indigenous rising with great force.

From 1937 it pushed Taiwanese to take Japanese names and speak Japanese, and many served in the war. In 1945 the island was handed to the Republic of China. Clashes with the new rulers led to the February 28 incident of 1947, and many older Taiwanese remembered Japanese rule more kindly than what came after.
sum: Japan ruled Taiwan as its first colony for fifty years, from the Treaty of Shimonoseki in 1895 to the end of the Second World War in 1945.
